title: Oddball Office Procedures: Handling Miscellaneous Situations
author: Asha Patel
content:
## Overview
This page documents a set of intentionally lightweight and occasionally whimsical procedures for small, real-world oddities that have occurred at Redwood Inference offices. The purpose is pragmatic: provide a repeatable, low-friction decision path for front-desk staff, people-ops, and any engineer who volunteers to handle the strange but non-critical situations that crop up.

These are not policies with legal force; they are pragmatic guidance and a place to capture low-risk defaults so we avoid ad-hoc escalation. Treat this page as an informal supplement to Office Guidelines.

## When to use this page
- The issue is non-safety-critical (no bodily harm, fire, major property damage).
- The situation is awkward, unexpected, and not covered by standard HR or security playbooks.
- You need a quick, sensible default to avoid micro-escalations (e.g., who takes custody of a found office cactus).

## Common scenarios and recommended handling (quick-reference)
1. Found items: keys, umbrellas, electronics
   - Put in the labeled "Found" basket at reception with date and finder initials.
   - Photograph item and post a single-line thread in #office-lost-and-found (photo + approximate location + date).
   - After 30 days unclaimed: donate (clothing) or recycle securely (storage devices) per IT disposal guidance.

2. A plant that clearly belongs to no one (the Rogue Plant)
   - Move it to the communal window bench and label with a sticky note: "Rogue Plant — survivor program."
   - If it’s thriving after 60 days and no owner identified, people-ops will adopt into the office green roster and assign a caretaker volunteer.

3. Persistent smell in the breakroom (non-emergency)
   - Ventilate windows/doors, check trash and forgotten food, log incident in the facilities queue.
   - If smell persists after two checks, escalate to facilities manager and note the date/time and area.

4. Small animal or insect guest (non-dangerous)
   - Safely trap or guide outside using a cup and paper or request facilities assistance.
   - For bees/wasps/large pests: do not attempt removal; contact facilities immediately.

## Step-by-step playbook: "Rogue Office Item"
1. Secure item and take a clear photo.
2. Label with date, finder initials, and a one-line description.
3. Place in reception "Found" basket or the secure bin for electronics.
4. Post notice in #office-lost-and-found with photo and location.
5. Record a 1-line note in the Facilities ticket system (ticket title: Found item — <short desc>).
6. After 30 days, follow disposal rules aligned to item type (electronics -> IT disposal; clothing -> donation).

## Table: Disposal guidelines (quick)
| Item type | Short-term home | 30-day outcome | Responsible owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Clothing | Found basket (closet shelf) | Donate | People-Ops |
| Keys / Wallets | Locked reception drawer | Security hold + attempt owner contact | Facilities |
| Electronics (phones, USB) | Secure bin (keyed) | IT erase / recycle | IT Ops |
| Houseplants | Communal bench | Assign caretaker or rehome | People-Ops |

## Communication templates
- Slack post (short): "Found a [item] near <location> at <time>. Photo attached. Putting it in reception. Please DM if it’s yours."
- Reception note (sticky): "Found: <item>. Date: <YYYY-MM-DD>. Finder: <initials>."

## Ownership and escalation
- Default owner for first 30 days: Reception / Facilities.
- If item appears high-value or clearly sensitive (e.g., labeled drives, encrypted devices): immediate escalation to IT and Security. Do not power on unknown devices.

## Related work and historical notes
- This page replaces a set of ad-hoc Google Docs that accumulated small anecdotes. It aims to reduce repeated ask/clarify cycles for reception staff.
- Past oddities that inspired this doc: a potted fern relocation, an unclaimed umbrella stash after a heavy rain day, and a mysterious jar of pickles left in a fridge (resolved by donation).

## Open questions / future items
- Should we add a short queue form for found electronics to capture serial numbers? (Tentative: yes — coordinate with IT.)
- Consider a quarterly "green roster" check to avoid plant turnover.

## Acknowledgements
Thanks to front-desk staff and the facilities volunteers for early feedback and for tolerating the majority of the experiments that motivated this page.

---
Notes: This page is intentionally light in formal language to encourage adoption. If an item is legally sensitive or safety-related, follow the standard incident or HR process instead of this guidance.
